rules: Never impede traffic — park fully in pull-offs or keep moving. Emergency vehicles must be able to pass at all times; this is the permitting agencies' #1 issue.
If the runner drops, they MUST report to an aid station captain (or text the RD) before leaving the course. THIS IS CRITICAL.
No crewing, spectating, or pacing at ANY below-rim aid station — all crew zones are on top of the Rim.
Runners share the forest roads (Rim Rd/FS-300, FS-321, FS-393, Milk Ranch Point Rd) — drive slowly and minimize dust.
Rim Road is scenic but has hairpin turns and blind corners with 1,000-ft drops just off the edge. High clearance is nice; 4x4 not needed.
No facilities once you leave Pine/Payson for the Rim — pack food, water, and warm layers for a full day and night.
crew_info.cell_strategy: Best cell signal is near the edge of the Rim; there is NO service at Buck Springs, General Springs, or Dickerson Flat. Wait in a pull-off within signal to watch live timing (live.aravaiparunning.com — updates can lag), then drive in when your runner nears.

station_notes.Black Mesa: Crews-only zone spanning ~3 mi of Rim Road between Horton Creek and Babe Haught trails. Stop only in pull-offs, never on the road itself. NO parking or crewing at the Horton aid station just east of the zone.
station_notes.Buck Springs: From Rim Road turn onto FS-321 and continue ~3 mi; the aid is on the right. Runners are on FS-321/Rim Rd the entire way — drive slow. No cell at the aid; consider waiting in a pull-off on FS-300 in signal.
station_notes.General Springs: From Pine: AZ-87 north 14.5 mi to the Rim Road turnoff, Rim Road 12 mi to the powerlines, then left down FS-393 to the cabin (~1/3 mi). Runners are on this road — caution at the turn. No cell at the cabin (manual: ~1h16m from Pine).
station_notes.Dickerson Flat: From AZ-87 continue STRAIGHT onto Milk Ranch Point Rd — do NOT turn left onto Rim Road. 1.2 mi to a Y (stay right), then 1.7 mi to Turkey Springs TH. Crew only in the immediate trailhead area; do not block the roadway. No cell service.
station_notes.Pine Trailhead: Under 1 mi from town, no extended parking — quick stop only. A pacer may join here for the final ~2 mi.
station_notes.Finish: Pine Town Ramada / Community Center on the main road through Pine; parking surrounds the area, food within walking distance.

crew_info.start_notes: Park at the Old Pine Parking Area (vehicles may stay all weekend; free dispersed camping). Two-Sixty TH is DROP-OFF ONLY — no parking at the start. Runner shuttles leave Old Pine at 4:25a and 4:40a.
crew_info.driving: See the official Crew Guide for driving directions; never block forest roads.

coach_notes.terrain: Climbs the Mogollon Rim 6× over 102.6 mi and 15,900 ft. Technical tread on Highline / Donahue / Myrtle / Promontory; the rim climbs are long and the canyon descents are steep and rocky. The limiting factor late in this race is musculoskeletal — quads on the rim descents, feet, connective tissue — not aerobic fitness, so durability and eccentric load are the training targets.
coach_notes.climate: Mid-September on the Rim: the below-rim canyons can run 80 °F+ in the afternoon while the nights on top get genuinely cold. Heat is one of the three wildcards and a heat block belongs in the build-out; the overnight asks for real layers.
coach_notes.altitude: The course runs between about 5,300 ft and 7,912 ft, most of it on the Rim near 7,000 ft. For an athlete training at ~5,300 ft in Albuquerque this is a mild stressor rather than a limiter — it shows up as a slightly lower ceiling on the climbs, not as acclimatization work.
coach_notes.key_demands: ~30+ hours at very low intensity. Time-on-feet durability, deliberate race-effort simulation days (hike the climbs, relaxed shuffle elsewhere, fueling at the kcal/h target, race gear and poles), back-to-back long days when one huge day will not fit the calendar, a night section rehearsed, and a fueling plan that survives a day and a half. Heat, altitude and technical descent are the real wildcards.
coach_notes.race_week: Race week is week 20 of the block — taper proportional to the build, course rec near peak rather than in race week, 06:00 start on Saturday 2026-09-12 with a 38 h cutoff. Runner shuttles leave Old Pine at 04:25 and 04:40.

aid_stations.source: tt-yib.2 migration from config/race-course.json — Hand-authored from the 2025 Mogollon Monster 100 runner manual aid chart + the StravaGPX route. Segment miles/cutoff hours are 2025 values and may shift when the 2026 manual drops — this file is the single editable source. build-course.mjs snaps each aid station to the GPX track and treats course.json as the Race views' source of truth (state.json race object is left untouched). NOTE: the 2025 chart's 'total elapsed hours' column contradicts its own bold cutoff clock times (by up to 1h45m); cutoff_h here is derived from the posted CLOCK times (start 6:00 AM), which are what aid captains enforce.
